DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

english.notes:
(i) The date of the offence is the actual date of death.
(ii) The rule that death must follow within a year and a day applies to acts or omissions before 16th September 1996.
(iii) The rule is abolished for acts or omissions on or after that date which result in death. See - Abolition - 'year and a day rule'.
(iv) The consent of the Attorney General is required where:
(a) the injury was sustained more than three years before death; OR
(b) the accused has been previously convicted of the offence alleged to be connected with the death.
(v) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.
(vi) See section 72 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales.
